props.gloss_en: one who traps a deer that is blind or asleep is liable
[one who traps a deer that is] lame, old or sick is exempt
Abaye to Rav Yosef: what is different about these, and what about those?
Rav Yosef: these [the blind and sleeping] are prone to struggle [to escape]
Rav Yosef: those [the lame, old and sick] are not prone to struggle
the other baraita: [one who traps] a sick [deer] is liable
Rav Sheshet: this [the baraita making him liable] is of a deer sick with fever
Rav Sheshet: that [the baraita exempting him] is of a deer sick with exhaustion
R' Meir: one who traps locusts, cicadas, hornets or mosquitoes on Shabbat is liable
the Sages: [one who traps] any whose kind is trapped is liable
the Sages: and any whose kind is not trapped -- exempt
one who traps locusts at the time of dew is exempt
at the time of heat -- liable
Elazar ben Mehavai: if they were swarming, [one who traps them is] exempt

a dilemma: does Elazar ben Mehavai's statement stand on the first clause [dew] or on the last [heat]? (Steinsaltz: on the first, a stringency -- liable in dew unless swarming; on the last, a leniency -- exempt in heat when swarming)
resolved: Elazar ben Mehavai stands on the last clause -- even at the time of heat, swarming locusts are exempt
the תא שמע baraita, Elazar ben Mehavai: even at the time of heat, if they were swarming -- exempt
